name: How does the local Colorado climate affect interior trim installation?

mainEntity.name: How does the local Colorado climate affect interior trim installation?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Denver metro area, seasonal shifts between cold, dry winter air and warm, humid summer conditions cause interior framing and trim to expand and contract. If wood trim is installed immediately after delivery without acclimatizing inside the home, joints can open up or buckle within months. In addition, expansive clay soils in areas like Aurora, Centennial, and Parker can cause minor home settling that throws door jambs and wall corners out of square. Finish carpenters must use flexible caulking, proper fastener patterns, and thorough acclimation to keep trim seams tight year-round.
acceptedAnswer.description: Denver's dry winters and seasonal humidity shifts cause wood to expand and contract. Trim must acclimate to the home's indoor humidity before fastening to prevent separated joints.
